beats.text: The dramatic moment at ECCV 2012 when AlexNet outperformed the second-place handcrafted model by an unthinkable 10.8 percentage points.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen showing a complex, messy hand-drawn diagram on the left and a clean, glowing neural network on the right.

beats.text: The villain? Handcrafted feature engineering. It was a fragile. Manual bottleneck that couldn't scale to the complexity of real-world vision.
beats.visual_focus: A single human hand trying to sort thousands of tiny, blurry image fragments into folders.

beats.text: AlexNet pivoted to hierarchical feature mapping. It learned to stack simple edges into complex shapes automatically. Layer by layer.
beats.visual_focus: A 3D stack of layers where pixels transform into edges, then textures, then recognizable objects.

beats.text: Using ReLU activation and max-pooling. It bypassed the vanishing gradient trap. It forced the GPU to learn, not just compute.
beats.visual_focus: A code snippet highlighting F.relu and F.max_pool2d, with data flowing through the layers like water.

beats.text: The result? A 15.3% error rate. It crushed the competition by a massive 10.8 percentage points. The era of deep learning began.
beats.visual_focus: A bar chart showing AlexNet at 15.3% towering over the 26.1% baseline.
